The CDC’s “Trend (All Years Available)” section of the *Experiencing Violence* part of the Youth Risk Behavior Survey Data Summary & Trends Report 2013‑2023 does not appear in the sources that were accessed in this investigation. Consequently, the specific four behaviors that the report lists as “trending in the wrong direction” cannot be identified from the evidence collected.

**What the evidence does provide**

| Section (Experiencing Violence) | Trend (2013‒2023) – from the South Dakota PDF (illustrative trend data) |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Physical dating violence        | 7.8 % → 10.0 % (increase) |
| Sexual dating violence          | 10.5 % → 12.7 % (increase) |
| Ever touched/sexually pinched   | 22.9 % → 28.6 % (increase) |
| Electronic bullying             | 17.8 % → 19.0 % (increase) |
| Not going to school because of unsafe | 5.2 % → 8.8 % (increase) |
| Threatened/injured with weapon on school property | 5.0 % → 9.5 % (increase) |
| Physical fight on school property | 6.6 % → 7.4 % (increase) |
| Bullying on school property    | 24.3 % → 26.8 % (increase) |

These data show which behaviors have increased over time, but the CDC report’s own selection of the “four areas trending in the wrong direction” is not present in the consulted source and therefore cannot be confirmed.
